20  Swiss Re Institute sigma  No 1/2025  Insurability and homeowner insurance in the US
The surge in construction and rebuilding costs adversely impacted underwriting results 
in property insurance. From 2020 to 2024, the segment’s combined ratio was more 
than 100%, reaching a decade high of 1 10% in 2023. This indicates that insurers paid 
out more in claims and expenses than they collected in premiums (see Figure 13). 41  On a 
net basis, homeowner insurers have incurred underwriting losses of USD 35 billion over 
the last 10 years. They experienced underwriting profit in just three of those years.
Recent increases in homeowner premiums represent a catch-up effect to inflation gains, 
although with a lag due to reporting and regulatory processes. After several years of 
underwriting losses, homeowners’ premiums only recently caught up with housing 
replacement costs. However, ongoing underwriting losses suggest that premiums are 
still not commensurate with the risk, and that further alignment is necessary to sustain 
insurance business.
